reader.requirement: At --std 85, within a statement that contains another, the containing statement's next phrase (ELSE of IF, WHEN of EVALUATE/SEARCH, NOT AT END of READ, NOT ON SIZE ERROR, WITH DATA of RECEIVE, ELSE after a CALL ON OVERFLOW) must terminate the scope of any unterminated contained statement, including the 1985-only CALL ON OVERFLOW and RECEIVE NO DATA/WITH DATA phrases.

edition-consulted.switches: hands the target edition to ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Associates

ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(edition, f.Construct) admits a format carrying a construct; the only one is CALL's ON OVERFLOW format (Constructs.CallOnOverflowRemoved2023), available at 85 and not at 2023
Check(CallOnOverflowRemoved2023): refuses CALL ON OVERFLOW at 2023 (COBOL0882), passes at 85

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: CALL ... ON OVERFLOW is a phrase of the containing CALL at 85 (so a following ELSE ends its imperative statement) and is refused at 2023 (COBOL0882); every other phrase association takes the same arm
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses are 2023-written; not exercised at 85: CALL ON OVERFLOW ended by ELSE, RECEIVE NO DATA ended by WITH DATA and the RECEIVE ended by ELSE, SEARCH AT END ended by WHEN, READ AT END ended by NOT AT END

probes.printed: G2-SIZE, G2-INELSE, G2-OUTELSE2, G2-EV1, G2-EVW2, G2-SB, G2-SAE, G2-RAE, G2-N=7, G2-OVF, G2-SE (at --std 2023 the same source is refused: COBOL0882 CALL ON OVERFLOW was removed)
probes.expected: each ELSE/WHEN/NOT phrase ends the contained statement and continues the containing one: no -WRONG line; CALL of a missing program takes ON OVERFLOW and the ELSE belongs to the IF
WITH DATA ends the NO DATA imperative statement and ELSE ends the RECEIVE: first RECEIVE has a message (WD1), second has none (ND2)

probes.printed: error COBOL2796 (x3): EVALUATE WHEN / SEARCH WHEN: this IF statement is written without its explicit scope terminator END-IF, so it is a conditional statement, and the operand of this phrase is an imperative-statement
probes.expected: refused: 1985 EVALUATE and SEARCH WHEN take imperative-statement, and an IF without END-IF is conditional

probes.printed: error COBOL2269: ACCEPT ON EXCEPTION ... the phrase may be syntactically associated with no statement open here
probes.expected: refused at 85: a device ACCEPT has no exception phrase in 1985, so the phrase belongs to no open statement

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.4.4 GR2  (4.4.4 Explicit and Implicit Scope Terminators)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: The conditionalPhrases loop asks the innermost open statement first and ends it when the phrase is not its own, which is GR2's implicit termination; IF's ELSE, EVALUATE/SEARCH WHEN and the RECEIVE phrases are grammar positions that end the preceding statementBlock. The edition only decides CALL ON OVERFLOW's ownership, and at 85 it is owned, as the 1985 CALL format prints it.

refuter.evidence: Probes under refute-1985-088/src at --std 85. p4d (run p4d-001): ELSE ends a contained READ ... AT END ... NOT AT END inside an IF, printing R-NAE REC1 and then R-AE; ELSE ends a contained SEARCH AT END/WHEN (S-C); ELSE ends a contained STRING ON OVERFLOW/NOT ON OVERFLOW (ST-OVF); ELSE after an unexecuted STRING ON OVERFLOW (ST2-ELSE); no -WRONG line. 1985 format arms: p4c (CALL ... ON OVERFLOW ... NOT ON OVERFLOW) was refused with COBOL2269, and p4b (CALL ... ON OVERFLOW ... NOT ON EXCEPTION, mixing the two 1985 CALL formats) was refused with COBOL2269. p4a was refused with COBOL2796 for an unterminated CALL ON OVERFLOW used as STRING's ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement and for ADD ON SIZE ERROR used as READ AT END's imperative-statement; 1985 requires imperative-statement there, so the refusals are correct, and GR2 can end a contained conditional statement only under an IF's ELSE. The diagnostics quote §2023 text, which is wording, not this rule. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.4.4 GR2 the text is in GR2.
